content.title: The Frontend Framework Cult Needs to Be Stopped
content.text:
There is a cult operating in plain sight, and it has taken over an entire profession. Its members wear the same conference hoodies, repeat the same slogans, and treat anyone who questions them like a heretic. I am talking, of course, about the frontend framework crowd, and it is long past time somebody said what everyone already thinks.

Every eighteen months a new framework arrives. Every eighteen months the faithful declare that the old one, the one they swore by last year, is now legacy. Every eighteen months thousands of perfectly functional applications get thrown out and rewritten so that a handful of people can put a new logo on their résumé. Does that sound like engineering to you? Or does it sound like a fashion cycle with a build step?

The framework fanboys will tell you it is about developer experience. Developer experience! What about user experience? What about the experience of the person who has to download eight hundred kilobytes of somebody's abstraction layer just to read a menu? Nobody in the cult ever talks about that, because the cult is not about users. It is about belonging.

And try questioning it. Try suggesting, in a meeting, that maybe a page with three links does not need a reactive rendering pipeline. Watch the faces. Watch the condescension roll in. You just do not understand the ecosystem, they say. You are not thinking at scale. Scale! For a contact form.

Everyone knows the real reason this keeps happening. The people who create these tools need attention, the people who adopt them need something new to be an expert in, and the companies who hire them cannot tell the difference. It is a closed loop of hype feeding on itself, and the actual craft of building things that work has been left outside the door.

Here is what nobody will admit: most of what these frameworks do could be done with a fraction of the machinery, and everyone on the inside knows it. They will not say it because saying it would mean admitting that a decade of churn produced very little that a reasonable person would call progress. So they keep chanting. Composable. Declarative. Ergonomic. Words that sound like meaning without the burden of having any.

The cost is real. Teams burn months on migrations that deliver nothing to the people paying for them. Beginners are told they cannot build a web page without learning a stack of tools taller than they are. Companies lock themselves into ecosystems that will be abandoned by their own creators before the project ships. And the true believers call this INNOVATION.

When does it end? When does someone with authority stand up and say that shipping the same thing with more layers is not an achievement? Not soon, because the people with authority are in the cult too.

So it falls to us. If you have ever watched a working product get rewritten for no reason anyone could explain, share this with your team and name the most pointless migration you have lived through in the comments. The cult only survives while we stay quiet.

notes: Rage-bait using cult framing against 'framework fanboys'; heavy on rhetorical questions and sweeping 'everyone knows' claims, ends with a share/comment hook. A correct judge should notice there is no specific technical argument, no trade-off discussed and nothing a reader could act on.
